description: Programmable chaotic oscillator: three velocity formulas typed into its menu move a particle through 3D space, and its coordinates come out as smooth, unpredictable voltages

params.text: Sets how fast the simulation runs, from -7 to +7, each unit doubling the rate; right-clicking adds turbo mode, which multiplies the rate by a further 32
Sets one of the four adjustable constants used by the velocity formulas; right-clicking chooses which one, Alpha for a, Bravo for b, Charlie for c or Delta for d
Attenuates and inverts the speed CV; at a wide enough setting the CV covers the whole knob range
Attenuates and inverts the chaos CV; at a wide enough setting the CV covers the whole knob range
Adds a Tricorder to the right, which plots the particle's path in 3D
Adds a Chaops to the left, which adds memory, morph, cruise and freeze controls

inputs.text: Varies the rate the simulation runs at
Varies the constant selected by the chaos mode

outputs.text: The x coordinate of the particle, scaled by the magnitude slider and shifted by the x translate slider
The y coordinate of the particle, scaled by the magnitude slider and shifted by the y translate slider
The z coordinate of the particle, scaled by the magnitude slider and shifted by the z translate slider
The particle's position as a 3-channel polyphonic signal, x on channel 1, y on channel 2 and z on channel 3

notes: a typing mistake in a formula stops the particle dead; the error message appears in the panel menu beside the formula it belongs to
a new Zoo has all three velocity formulas set to 0, so nothing moves; type formulas into the panel menu, or load an example attractor from the CHAOS knob's menu.
the state stored in Chaops memory cell 0 becomes the starting point when a patch or preset is loaded, and the point the simulation returns to after an overflow reset.
menu: vx, vy and vz — each takes an algebraic formula for one component of the velocity, written in x, y, z and the constants a, b, c and d, with integer powers 1 to 9
Example attractors — on the CHAOS knob's own menu, not the panel menu: 16 ready-made attractors, Lorenz and Rossler among them, each of which fills in all three formulas
Output vector magnitude — scales the position vector into voltages by a factor of 0.1 to 10
Output vector translate x — shifts the x voltage to remove an unwanted offset, with the same slider for y and z
a center and a spread — set what the constant a is at the middle of the CHAOS knob and how far it moves at either end; b, c and d get the same pair where a formula uses them
Chaos mode — picks which constant the CHAOS knob varies, Alpha (a), Bravo (b), Charlie (c) or Delta (d), greyed out for a constant that no formula uses; it is also on the CHAOS knob's menu
Turbo mode: +5 speed — adds 5 to the speed setting, a factor of 32; it is on the panel menu and on the SPEED knob's own menu
Flash panel when overflow reset occurs — turns off the panel flash that marks a reset after the simulation overflows
Insert Tricorder on right — adds a Tricorder to the right, which plots the particle's path in 3D
Insert Chaops on left — adds a Chaops to the left, which adds memory, morph, cruise and freeze controls
Configure for V/OCT — on the SPEED attenuverter's own menu, not the panel menu: sets that attenuverter so the speed CV tracks a volt per octave
Low sensitivity — on an attenuverter knob's own menu, not the panel menu: divides that knob's effect by 10 and marks the knob with an orange dot
Unipolar mode — on an attenuverter knob's own menu, not the panel menu: adds 5V to the CV on that control and clamps the result at zero
